detections.ruleName: Hidden cross-origin iframe inserted after load
detections.significance: In the documented chain, selected devices received code that inserted a 1x1 frame to load the next stage. A hidden frame alone is common; together with a preceding ad-selection request it matches that step.
detections.summary: A hidden cross-origin iframe was inserted after load.

alternativeExplanations: A viewability, verification or cookie-sync frame inserted by an ordinary ad.
A consent or login helper frame.
detections.confidenceRationale: A hidden cross-origin frame was observed, but no ad-selection request preceded it in the same frame lineage, and such frames are common in ordinary advertising.

evidence.observed: The page sensor observed a hidden cross-origin iframe targeting pixel.rubiconproject.com inserted 1012 ms after the frame loaded in a frame on sync.connectad.io.

limitations: Page signals come from an opt-in content script in sub-frames and report structural facts only (element kind, size class, target hostname); page text, cookie values and full URLs are never collected.
A hostile page can suppress or imitate these DOM signals; absence of a signal is not evidence that nothing happened, and a signal alone does not show what the inserted element did.
missingVisibility: What code actually executed inside the page, and its effect on the device, is not observed; only network metadata and, where enabled, bounded analysis of selected response text are available.
recommendedActions: Review the listed events and the cited research before drawing conclusions.
